title: Telemetry Fan-in Gateway for Inference KPI Ingest
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
We need a resilient telemetry "fan-in" gateway that consolidates Prometheus scrapes, OTLP metric streams, and lightweight ingestion from edge SDKs into a single canonical pipeline for Redwood inference KPIs. Current gaps: (1) duplicate and inconsistent label/attribute naming across exporters; (2) bursty spikes from many short-lived inference hosts causing Prometheus scrape failures and write amplification; (3) inability to apply deterministic enrichment and schema validation before metrics reach downstream storage. The gateway will provide buffering, attribute canonicalization, schema validation for custom inference KPIs (latency_p50/95/99, token_throughput, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_histogram), lightweight deduplication, and per-tenant rate controls. It must emit both Prometheus-compatible exposition for our long-term TSDB and OTLP/OTel for tracing correlation.

Design goals: highly-available, horizontally scalable, idempotent ingestion, minimal added latency (tail <50ms for telemetry path), clear observability of gateway health, and seamless fallback to direct ingestion if gateway is degraded.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts Prometheus remote write and OTLP metric streams concurrently and normalizes them into the canonical KPI schema.
Attribute canonicalizer maps known attribute variants to standard labels (model_name, region, deployment, route) with a configurable mapping file stored in S3.
Ingest buffer persists short bursts (up to 60s of median burst traffic) and exposes backlog metrics; backlog > threshold triggers autoscale events.
End-to-end tests show no telemetry data loss for 99.9% of simulated load with 1000 hosts emitting at 1req/s each.
Dashboards: new Gateway overview + KPI health panel added to Console with p50/p95/p99 latency derived from normalized metrics and a KV cache hit-rate panel.
Rollout plan validated via canary (5% traffic) with automatic rollback on gateway error rate >1% or ingestion latency >200ms.
Docs and runbook updated (Confluence + runbook on-call playbook) and a PR merged for sample SDK config.
Security review completed if customer tenants require PII-free ingest (flagged but false for initial delivery).
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Build a thin HTTP/GRPC front-end supporting Prometheus remote_write and OTLP/OTLPgRPC; metric translation module to convert Prom remote_write protobuf -> internal OTLP-like envelope.
Phase 2: Implement attribute canonicalizer + simple schema registry for KPI metric names and expected label sets. Mapping file stored in S3 and hot-reloadable.
Phase 3: Add in-memory write-behind buffer with optional persisted segments (local SSD) for burst durability; surface backlog and disk-usage metrics.
Phase 4: Integrate with routing layer to apply tenant-level rate limits and dynamic batching rules (per model/route), emit Prom-compatible exposition for scraping by our TSDB ingestion tier.
Phase 5: End-to-end tests, chaos injection (network partitions, disk full), and benchmark at scale in staging cluster.
Phase 6: Canary rollout with 5% of traffic, monitor SLA gates, iterate on mapping rules, then full rollout with a phased increase over 72 hours.
Phase 7: Post-rollout: decommission legacy direct exporters (opt-in) and provide migration docs and SDK snippets for customers.
PRs: gateway service, canonicalizer, mapping config, e2e test harness, console dashboard JSON net-new panels.
risks: Incorrect attribute mappings could cause metric cardinality explosion or silent metric fragmentation — mitigate via canary and mapping preview tool.
Persistent buffer storage failure could drop bursts — mitigation: replicate buffer segments across two nodes and surface high-severity alerts.
Adding the gateway could add observable latency — limit path criticality by keeping telemetry ingestion asynchronous from inference datapath and set SLOs for gateway latency.
Unexpected Prometheus remote_write variants from third-party exporters — add a compatibility test matrix and heuristics for unknown label sets.
testing_and_qa: Unit tests for translation module (prom_remote_write -> KPI envelope) with fuzz inputs.
Integration tests: OTLP producer -> gateway -> TSDB sink verifying label normalization and metric values.
Load tests in staging at 3x expected peak (simulate 10k hosts @ 2req/s).
Chaos: kill front-end pods, corrupt mapping file, and ensure automated rollback triggers work as expected.
Manual verification: dashboard panels show stable p50/p95/p99 and KV cache hit_rate aligns with runtime-provided telemetry within 2%.
Security scan: static secret scanning and minimal privileges for mapping-file S3 role.
monitoring_and_alerting: Gateway health: target 99.95% ingestion availability; alerts for ingestion_errors/sec > 5 or backlog_seconds > 60.
Metric-quality alerts: newly detected label cardinality increase > 5x for a metric name triggers investigation.
SLOs: telemetry ingest latency p95 < 150ms; p99 < 300ms; breach opens incident channel and triggers rollback if persistent > 15m.
Dashboards: Gateway overview, KPI normalization explorer, and metric-cardinality heatmap added to Console.
migration_notes: Provide a migration checklist for teams: verify mapping for model_name/model, opt-in to gateway by updating exporter endpoint to gateway DNS.
Offer 'passthrough' mode for first 48h to compare counts between direct ingestion and gateway-normalized metrics.
Deprecation timeline: 30-day opt-in window, then start redirecting low-volume tenants automatically with opt-out for enterprise customers.
